summary.title: Paper in 3 Minutes
keyPoints: The rTAPP procedure follows a reproducible sequence of steps
Video-based learning shows dynamic anatomy as it unfolds during surgery
Each procedural step builds on proper execution of the previous step
Tissue handling and plane development are demonstrated in motion
Understanding the sequence prevents disorientation during the case
summary.clinicalPearl: Surgical anatomy is dynamic. Structures move and change appearance with dissection - video captures this in a way static images cannot.

figures.caption: Step 1: Initial peritoneal incision and entry into preperitoneal space
figures.description: The lateral-to-medial peritoneal incision begins the development of the preperitoneal flap

figures.caption: Step 2: Identification of the inverted-Y landmarks
figures.description: Progressive dissection reveals the vas deferens and spermatic vessels

figures.caption: Step 3: Parietalization of the cord
figures.description: Separation of cord structures from the peritoneum

figures.caption: Step 4: Achievement of Critical View
figures.description: All four quadrants of the MPO are visualized

figures.caption: Step 5: Mesh placement and positioning
figures.description: Proper mesh orientation and coverage of the MPO

activities.title: Order the Procedural Steps
activities.instruction: Arrange the following steps in the correct surgical sequence

activities.title: Identify Key Moments
activities.instruction: Watch the video and mark when each milestone is achieved

flashcards.front: What is the first landmark to identify after entering the preperitoneal space?
flashcards.back: The inferior epigastric vessels (IEV). They orient all subsequent dissection.

flashcards.front: In which direction should the peritoneal flap be developed?
flashcards.back: Lateral to medial, creating adequate space for mesh placement.
Clear visualization of the inverted-Y with vas and vessels completely separated from peritoneum.
Only after achieving the Critical View of the Myopectineal Orifice (CV-MPO).

flashcards.front: What is the final step before closing ports?
flashcards.back: Complete peritoneal closure to prevent mesh-bowel contact.

questions.question: What is the correct order of: (A) Parietalize cord, (B) Identify IEV, (C) Achieve CV-MPO?
questions.explanation: Correct order: Identify IEV first, then parietalize cord, then achieve CV-MPO.

questions.question: Peritoneal closure should occur:
questions.explanation: Peritoneal closure is the final step after mesh is placed and fixed.

questions.question: Mesh fixation should be performed:
options: After achieving CV-MPO and placing mesh
questions.explanation: Mesh fixation follows mesh placement, which follows CV-MPO achievement.

questions.question: The peritoneal flap is developed:
questions.explanation: The flap is developed lateral to medial to create space for mesh.

questions.question: Why is understanding sequence important in rTAPP?
options: Each step depends on proper execution of previous steps
questions.explanation: Each procedural step builds on correct execution of the previous step.

takeaways: The rTAPP procedure follows a specific, reproducible sequence
Each step builds on proper execution of the previous step
Video demonstrates dynamic anatomy that static images cannot capture
pitfalls: Attempting mesh placement before completing parietalization
Skipping the CV-MPO check under time pressure
